title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ROCCO'S CHAIR
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Rocco Benedetti, a sixty-four-year-old barber in Elizabeth, New Jersey.
For thirty-eight years, he has cut hair on Elmora Avenue, and never once smiled for a photo.
Then a fancy new beard studio opened right across the street.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE NEON SIGN
segments.quote: Don't worry about the world coming to an end today. It's already tomorrow in Australia.
segments.author: Charles M. Schulz
lines: Neon lights, free espresso, and a young barber named Jayden with a beard like a hedge.
Rocco's chairs sat empty. At two a.m., he lay awake, sure he would close.
His wife Connie rolled over and quoted Charles Schulz, the man who drew Peanuts:
Don't worry about the world coming to an end today. It's already tomorrow in Australia.
Rocco laughed so hard he woke the dog. Then he slept.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CANNOLI
segments.quote: If you want to gather honey, don't kick over the beehive.
segments.author: Dale Carnegie
lines: Next morning, he painted a window sign: Real barbers don't serve lattes.
His old customer Sal read it, shook his head, and quoted Dale Carnegie:
If you want to gather honey, don't kick over the beehive.
So Rocco scraped off the sign, bought cannoli, and walked across the street to say welcome.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: KIDS THESE DAYS
segments.quote: Each generation imagines itself to be more intelligent than the one that went before it, and wiser than the one that comes after it.
segments.author: George Orwell
lines: Inside, he muttered about tattoos and music too loud. Kids these days.
Then he remembered his father yelling about his sideburns in nineteen seventy-nine.
He thought of a line from George Orwell:
Each generation imagines itself to be more intelligent than the one that went before it, and wiser than the one that comes after it.
He stopped, and asked Jayden how he got that fade so clean.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE FADE
segments.quote: Every man I meet is my master in some point, and in that I learn of him.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: Jayden showed him. Rocco's first try made a customer look like a pineapple.
He almost gave up. Then he thought of Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Every man I meet is my master in some point, and in that I learn of him.
So every Monday, Rocco crossed the street with coffee and learned.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE RAZOR
segments.quote: One starts to get young at the age of sixty, and then it's too late.
segments.author: Pablo Picasso
lines: Then Jayden asked a favor. Nobody had taught him a straight razor shave.
Rocco hesitated. Then he laughed and quoted the painter Pablo Picasso:
One starts to get young at the age of sixty, and then it's too late.
Not for me, he said. Now they teach a free Thursday class together.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE COMB-OVER
segments.quote: The best mirror is an old friend.
segments.author: George Herbert
lines: One night, Sal sat in Rocco's chair and pointed at Rocco's comb-over.
Forty years I've been your friend. That comb-over fools nobody.
Connie quoted the English writer George Herbert:
The best mirror is an old friend.
So Jayden shaved it clean. Rocco looked in the mirror, and smiled for the photo.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Rest easy. Make friends. Laugh at yourself. Learn. Teach. Hear the truth.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Rest easy. Bring cannoli, not signs. Laugh at yourself. Learn. Teach. Listen to old friends.
Rocco and I now share the same hairstyle. Mine took less work.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
